newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah softer in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah softer in late trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was softer against the dollar in late trading after driving up earlier on the back of a baht recovery, dealers said.

Regional currencies were initially dragged up by the baht as optimism about an impending rescue package for Thailand's ailing economy spread through the region. But early gains were eroded after the Thai baht gave up its initial gains.
One U.S. bank dealer said offshore sentiment on the rupiah was quite bullish in the morning, coupled with regional rebounds, until they met strong local support for dollars.
Spot rupiah was at 2,575/80 at 0900 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,575/85. It rose to a high of 2,560 in the morning.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,585.25/90.25 and 2,571.0/75.0, respectively.
One dealer attributed the strong local appetite for dollars to expensive overnight dollar deposit rates, traded at 13.0/14.0 percent late in the afternoon, but already on the uptrend since Monday.
"We could have seen the dollar falling below the 2,550 support level if local buying wasn't that strong," he said, adding the rupiah was, however, on the way to recovery.
The U.S. bank dealer said the rupiah was likely to test the 2,550 level by the end of the week if dollar liquidity eased.
The central bank continued with its recent policy of keeping short-term money relatively expensive and remained absent from the short-term securities market (SBPUs).

The bank offered one-to-three-day bilateral SBIs at 14.0 percent, one-week at 10.0 percent, two-week at 10.5 percent, one-month at 11.125 percent, three at 11.0, six at 11.625 and one-year at 12.25 percent.
Overnight rupiah was at 14.5/15.0 percent. Dealers said there were still some "anomalies" in the market following recent turbulence in the foreign exchange market.
Dealers said a combination of factors caused the short-dated swaps to fall while short-term money was on the rise and dollar liquidity was tight.
One Japanese bank dealer said the condition was only temporary and things would normalise soon. Overnight swap was at -0.05/par and tom/next at -0.10/-0.05 points.

One dealer said local operators who sold dollars previously had to collect the U.S. currency now while on the other hand they were also doing arbitrage with the swap market to enjoy high overnight rates in the money market.
"This seem to have pushed overnight dollars higher as they also need dollars to buy swaps," the dealer said.
He said the cheap short-dated swaps could have resulted from operators' selling of swaps they had purchased earlier but reloaded on the market because they could not mobilise dollars.
"Besides, offshore players were also over supplied with swaps. Before they bought dollars they had gone long in swaps."
Dealers said swaps were falling across the board, suggesting further stabilisation in the swap market.
One-month swap was at 14.0/16.0, two at 28.0/35.0, three at 47.0/50.0 and six at 94.0/100.0 points.
The central bank kept its intervention band at 2,378/2,682 but lowered the conversion band to 2,559/2,607 on Tuesday from 2,571/2,619 on Monday.
-- Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364
